summary: A dense Vital Lacerda worker-placement game where you run an art gallery: acquiring artists and artwork, hosting exhibitions, managing an auction house, and building your reputation to draw wealthy visitors. It's a long, intricate puzzle of interlocking systems where every action ripples through several tracks at once.
praised: remarkable thematic integration of mechanisms with the art-dealing theme
high production values and clever board design
criticised: very long playtime and steep learning curve
heavy rules overhead and fiddly bookkeeping
downtime between turns at higher player counts
can feel more like solving a puzzle than competing with people

interaction.kind: worker placement with a shared art market
interaction.detail: Players place workers on a shared action board and buy/sell art through a common speculative market, so occupying a space or driving up an artist's price affects everyone else's options. Each player's own gallery and contracts are private, but the market and worker spaces are the shared contested resource.

subsystems: Gallery art dealing (buying, promoting, and selling art)
scoring.how_you_win: Run galleries, artists, and assistants to buy and sell art while building reputation and market position; once two of three end conditions (tickets, celebrity artists, visitors) are triggered the game finishes, everything converts to money, and the richest curator wins.
